'''Francisco Román Alarcón Suárez''' ({{IPA|es|fɾanˈθisk roˈman alaɾˈkon ˈswaɾeθ}}; born 21 April 1992), commonly known as '''Isco''' ({{IPA|es|ˈisko|}}), is a Spanish professional [[Association football|footballer]] who plays as an [[Midfielder|attacking midfielder]] or [[left winger]] for [[La Liga]] club [[Real Betis]], which he [[Captain (association football)|captains]], and the [[Spain national football team|Spain national team]].

Isco began his career at [[Valencia CF|Valencia]], playing mainly in [[Valencia CF Mestalla|its reserve team]], before joining [[Málaga CF|Málaga]] in 2011. His performances at Málaga earned him the [[Golden Boy (award)|Golden Boy]] award in 2012, and a €65&nbsp;million move to [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] in June 2013, with whom he won 19 major trophies including five [[UEFA Champions League]] titles, three La Liga titles, one [[Copa del Rey]] and four [[FIFA Club World Cup]] titles. He left Real Madrid at the end of the [[2021–22 Real Madrid CF season|2021–22 season]] and then joined [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]]. In December 2022, his contract was mutually terminated and he spent the rest of the season without a club, before joining Betis in July 2023.

Isco represented Spain at various youth levels, including at the [[Football at the 2012 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2012 Olympics]], and made his senior international debut in 2013, later taking part at the [[2018 FIFA World Cup]].

==Club career==
===Valencia===
Isco was born in [[Benalmadena, Spain|Benalmadena]], [[Province of Málaga|Málaga]], [[Andalusia]]. As a child he played for Atlético Benamiel.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/28259902|title=Charlie I'Anson: The only Englishman in Spain's elite|date=20 August 2014|access-date=4 November 2014|author=Neil Johnston|work=BBC Sport|archive-date=6 May 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160506104143/http://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/28259902|url-status=live}}</ref> A product of [[Valencia CF (youth)|Valencia]]'s youth system, he spent the [[2009–10 Segunda División B|2009–10 season]] with [[Valencia CF Mestalla|the club's reserve team]] in [[Segunda División B]], netting once in 26 games and suffering relegation.

While still registered with the reserves, Isco made his debut with the first team on 11 November 2010, against [[UD Logroñés|Logroñés]] in the [[2010–11 Copa del Rey]], scoring two goals in a 4–1 home win ([[Paco Alcácer]] made his senior debut in the same fixture).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.goal.com/es/match/54025/valencia-vs-ud-logro%C3%B1%C3%A9s/report|title=Copa del Rey: Isco y Vicente alegran la noche en Mestalla (4–1)|trans-title=Copa del Rey: Isco and Vicente light up night at Mestalla (4–1)|publisher=Goal.com|language=es|date=11 November 2010|access-date=7 February 2014|archive-date=1 May 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140501121234/http://www.goal.com/es/match/54025/valencia-vs-ud-logro%C3%B1%C3%A9s/report|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.valenciacf.com/ver/17802/a-octavos-4-1.html|title=A octavos (4–1)|trans-title=To the round-of-16 (4–1)|publisher=Valencia CF|language=es|date=11 November 2010|access-date=26 November 2018|archive-date=24 February 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140224041019/http://www.valenciacf.com/ver/17802/a-octavos-4-1.html/|url-status=live}}</ref> He played his first [[La Liga]] match three days later, featuring for 20 minutes in a 2–0 home win against [[Getafe CF|Getafe]] after coming on as a [[Substitute (association football)|substitute]] for [[Aritz Aduriz]];<ref>[http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/302022?cc=5739 Valencia get back to winning ways] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121024090842/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/302022?cc=5739 |date=24 October 2012 }}; ESPN Soccernet, 14 November 2010</ref> he thereafter made three further league appearances and two in the [[UEFA Champions League]], all from the bench,<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.bdfutbol.com/en/p/j300520.html?temp=2010-11 |title=Isco: Matches 2010–11 |website=BDFutbol |access-date=26 November 2018 }}</ref> and helped the B-team [[2011 Tercera División play-offs|return to the third level]] by scoring 15 goals in their campaign.<ref>{{Cite web |url=https://www.resultados-futbol.com/jugador/2011/Isco-44027 |title=Isco: Temporada 2010/2011 |language=es |website=Resultados Futbol |access-date=26 November 2018 |archive-date=14 January 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200114121656/https://www.resultados-futbol.com/jugador/2011/Isco-44027 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name=cumplido>{{Cite web |url=http://www.deportevalenciano.com/2011/05/29/objetivo-cumplido |title=Objetivo cumplido |trans-title=Objective complete |language=es |work=Deporte Valenciano |date=29 May 2011 |access-date=26 November 2018 |archive-date=26 November 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181126221631/http://www.deportevalenciano.com/2011/05/29/objetivo-cumplido |url-status=live }}</ref>

===Málaga===
In mid-July 2011, Isco moved back to his home province and signed a five-year contract with [[Málaga CF|Málaga]] after the club activated his [[Buyout clause|buy-out clause]] of €6&nbsp;million.<ref>[http://www.marca.com/2011/07/11/futbol/equipos/valencia/1310394247.html Isco firma cinco temporadas por el Málaga (Isco signs for five seasons with Málaga)] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120922094312/http://www.marca.com/2011/07/11/futbol/equipos/valencia/1310394247.html |date=22 September 2012 }}; ''[[Marca (newspaper)]]'', 11 July 2011 {{in lang|es}}</ref> He scored his first goal for his new team on 21 November 2011, starting in a 3–1 away win against [[Racing de Santander]];<ref>[http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/323917?cc=5739 Malaga up to fifth] {{Webarchive|url=https://archive.today/20120715081349/http://soccernet.espn.go.com/report/_/id/323917?cc=5739 |date=15 July 2012 }}; ESPN Soccernet, 21 November 2011</ref> he netted again the following week in a 2–1 win against [[Villarreal CF|Villarreal]],<ref>[http://www.goal.com/en-us/match/63038/malaga-vs-villarreal/report Malaga 2–1 Villarreal: Toulalan scores and is sent off as Manuel Pellegrini's men go fifth in La Liga] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120101185058/http://www.goal.com/en-us/match/63038/malaga-vs-villarreal/report |date=1 January 2012 }}; Goal.com, 28 November 2011</ref> and finished [[2011–12 La Liga|his first season]] with 32 games and five goals as the side qualified for the [[2012–13 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League]] for the first time in its history.

On 18 September 2012, in Málaga's first game in the Champions League group stage, Isco netted twice in a 3–0 home win over [[FC Zenit Saint Petersburg|Zenit]], also being chosen as [[Man of the Match]].<ref>[https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0201-0e7f1706a0b1-9602134c09f5-1000--magical-malaga-make-it-a-debut-to-remember/ Magical Málaga make it a debut to remember] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131016071422/http://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/season%3D2013/matches/round%3D2000347/match%3D2009500/postmatch/report/index.html |date=16 October 2013 }}; UEFA, 18 September 2012</ref> On 22 December he scored the first goal in an eventual 3–2 win against [[Real Madrid CF|Real Madrid]] at [[La Rosaleda Stadium|La Rosaleda]], leading the locals to their first victory over that opponent in 29 years;<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.goal.com/en/match/85324/malaga-vs-real-madrid-cf/report|title=Malaga 3–2 Real Madrid: Casillas dropped as beleaguered Blancos succumb to Santa Cruz double|publisher=Goal.com|date=22 December 2012|access-date=7 January 2013|archive-date=30 December 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121230185659/http://www.goal.com/en/match/85324/malaga-vs-real-madrid-cf/report|url-status=live}}</ref> in December he won the [[Golden Boy (award)|Golden Boy]] award, beating [[Stephan El Shaarawy]] and [[Thibaut Courtois]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.malagacf.com/es/noticia/isco-ganador-prestigioso-golden-boy-2012/69372|title=Isco, ganador del prestigioso Golden Boy|trans-title=Isco, winner of prestigious Golden Boy award|publisher=Málaga's official website|language=es|date=22 December 2012|access-date=4 April 2013|archive-date=29 May 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130529063212/http://www.malagacf.com/es/noticia/isco-ganador-prestigioso-golden-boy-2012/69372|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=https://bleacherreport.com/articles/1585120-20-most-improved-players-in-2012-13|title=Isco: Most Improved Players|publisher=Bleacher Report|author=Ed Dove|date=28 March 2013|access-date=7 April 2013|archive-date=2 April 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130402072905/http://bleacherreport.com/articles/1585120-20-most-improved-players-in-2012-13?|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 28 January 2013, Isco ended speculation regarding his future by signing a new contract with Málaga – his new buyout clause was set at €35&nbsp;million.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/11827/8451175/Isco-ends-speculation-regarding-future-by-penning-new-Malaga-contract|title=Isco ends speculation regarding future by penning new Malaga contract|publisher=[[Sky Sports]]|date=28 January 2013|access-date=28 January 2013}}</ref> He scored his eleventh goal of the campaign on 13 March, netting the opener in a 2–0 home win against [[FC Porto|Porto]], good enough for [[2012–13 UEFA Champions League knockout phase#Quarter-finals|last-eight]] qualification after the 0–1 first leg loss at the [[Estádio do Dragão]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0207-0e9efe194916-376483800444-1000--santa-cruz-sends-malaga-into-last-eight/|title=Santa Cruz sends Málaga into last eight|publisher=UEFA|date=13 March 2013|access-date=14 March 2013|archive-date=26 January 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220126062051/https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0207-0e9efe194916-376483800444-1000--santa-cruz-sends-malaga-into-last-eight/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2013/mar/13/malaga-porto-champions-league-match-report|title=Málaga cruise into Champions League quarter-finals after Porto are sunk|work=[[The Guardian]]|date=13 March 2013|access-date=13 March 2013|archive-date=5 October 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131005075309/http://www.theguardian.com/football/2013/mar/13/malaga-porto-champions-league-match-report|url-status=live}}</ref>

===Real Madrid===
On 17 June 2013, Isco confirmed that he had received offers from Real Madrid and former Málaga manager [[Manuel Pellegrini]]'s [[Manchester City F.C.|Manchester City]], but stated he would only make a final decision on his future after the [[2013 UEFA European Under-21 Championship Final|UEFA European Under-21 Championship final]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.goal.com/en-us/news/69/transfer-zone/2013/06/17/4054769/isco-reveals-city-and-madrid-offers|title=Isco reveals City and Madrid offers|publisher=Goal.com|date=17 June 2013|access-date=17 June 2013|archive-date=20 June 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130620221936/http://www.goal.com/en-us/news/69/transfer-zone/2013/06/17/4054769/isco-reveals-city-and-madrid-offers|url-status=live}}</ref> On 26 June, Real Madrid president Florentino Pérez confirmed that a deal had been reached with the player and that he would be presented by the club next week, once he passed his medical;<ref name="u21">{{cite web|url=http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/11679/8794449/Transfer-News-Real-Madrid-say-they-have-won-battle-to-sign-Isco|title=Transfer news: Real Madrid say they have won battle to sign Isco|publisher=Sky Sports|date=27 June 2013|access-date=27 June 2013|archive-date=28 June 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130628030812/http://www1.skysports.com/football/news/11679/8794449/Transfer-News-Real-Madrid-say-they-have-won-battle-to-sign-Isco|url-status=live}}</ref> the following day he signed a five-year contract, with Real Madrid paying €30&nbsp;million for his services, thus becoming the first signing of newly appointed manager [[Carlo Ancelotti]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/23083749|title=Isco: Real Madrid agree deal for Manchester City target|publisher=BBC|date=27 June 2013|access-date=27 June 2013|archive-date=4 February 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180204013707/http://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/23083749|url-status=live}}</ref>
[[File:Isco - Atletico Madrid 9.jpg|thumb|left|Isco with Real Madrid in 2013]]
On 18 August 2013 Isco made his official debut for the ''Merengues'', recording an [[Assist (football)|assist]] and scoring the winning goal in a 2–1 home win over [[Real Betis]], the latter coming through an 85th-minute header.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2013/aug/18/real-madrid-real-betis-isco|title=Real Madrid give Carlo Ancelotti winning start after Isco's dream debut|work=The Guardian|date=18 August 2013|access-date=19 August 2013|archive-date=3 August 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180803165105/https://www.theguardian.com/football/2013/aug/18/real-madrid-real-betis-isco|url-status=live}}</ref> He continued with his form by netting two goals against [[Athletic Bilbao]] on 1 September (3–1, also at the [[Santiago Bernabéu Stadium|Santiago Bernabéu]]).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.marca.com/eventos/marcador/futbol/2013_14/primera/jornada_3/rma_ath/|title=Progresa adecuadamente|trans-title=Steady progress|work=Marca|location=Spain|language=es|date=1 September 2013|access-date=1 September 2013|archive-date=3 August 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180803193954/http://www.marca.com/eventos/marcador/futbol/2013_14/primera/jornada_3/rma_ath/|url-status=live}}</ref>

[[File:Shahter-Reak M 2015 (13).jpg|180px|thumb|Isco playing for Real Madrid in 2015]]

In spite of continuing to score regularly when featured, Isco received limited opportunities in the first team due to the [[Formation (association football)|4–3–3 formation]] not being suited for his style, but Ancelotti stated that it was "a temporary problem".<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.goal.com/en-sg/news/3882/spain/2014/02/16/4622613/ancelotti-ronaldo-and-isco-are-unhappy|title=Ancelotti: Ronaldo and Isco are unhappy|publisher=Goal.com|date=16 February 2014|access-date=18 March 2014|archive-date=3 August 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180803194125/http://www.goal.com/en-sg/news/3882/spain/2014/02/16/4622613/ancelotti-ronaldo-and-isco-are-unhappy|url-status=live}}</ref> He scored 11 goals in 53 official games in [[2013–14 Real Madrid CF season|his first season]]. He played 61 minutes in the [[2014 UEFA Champions League Final|Champions League final]], a 4–1 win over [[Atlético Madrid]] in [[Lisbon]].<ref name="cl2014">{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/27383593|title=Real Madrid 4–1 Atlético Madrid|work=[[BBC Sport]]|date=24 May 2014|access-date=25 May 2014|archive-date=26 January 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160126180206/http://www.bbc.com/sport/0/football/27383593|url-status=live}}</ref>

Isco started the first game of the [[2014–15 La Liga|2014–15 season]] against [[Real Sociedad]], and scored the first in a 4–1 win against [[UD Almería|Almería]] on 12 December 2014.<ref>{{cite web |author1=PA Sport |title=Cristiano Ronaldo scores twice as Real Madrid hit four at Almeria |url=https://www.espn.com/football/report/_/gameId/402487 |website=[[ESPN]] |access-date=20 August 2025 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20250820025012/https://www.espn.com/football/report/_/gameId/402487 |archive-date=20 August 2025}}</ref> He was a regular starter in the club's [[FIFA Club World Cup]] [[2014 FIFA Club World Cup|winning campaign]], scoring the last in a 4–0 semi-final routing of [[Cruz Azul]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://prosoccertalk.nbcsports.com/2014/12/16/ronaldo-isco-combine-for-nifty-goal-in-real-madrids-4-0-club-world-cup-win-over-cruz-azul-video/|title=Ronaldo, Isco combine for nifty goal in Zidane]] by the French legend himself.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sportsmole.co.uk/football/real-madrid/news/zidane-isco-is-a-lot-like-me_199954.html|title=Zinedine Zidane: "Isco is a lot like crisis|url=http://www.marca.com/en/2015/11/21/en/football/real_madrid/1448122771.html|access-date=22 November 2015|work=Marca|location=Spain|date=21 November 2015|archive-date=3 August Isco was a part-time starter when the team won the [[2015–16 UEFA Champions League]] defeating Atlético Madrid 5–3 on penalties in [[2016 UEFA Champions League Final|the final]] played at the [[San Siro]] in [[Milan]], Italy.<ref name="cl2016">{{cite web|url = https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/022d-0e957c5979eb-37493cb53cd0-1000--spot-on-real-madrid-defeat-atletico-in-final-again/|title = Spot-on Real Madrid defeat Atlético in final again|date = 28 May 2016|publisher = UEFA|access-date = 22 March 2025|archive-date = 10 January 2018|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20180110225552/http://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/season=2016/matches/round=2000638/match=2015789/postmatch/report/index.html|url-status = live}}</ref>

He appeared 30 times during the 2016–17 season, as Real Madrid won the [[2016–17 La Liga|La Liga]] title;<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.laliga.es/noticias/real-madrid-campeon-de-laliga-santander-2016-17|title=El Real Madrid, campeón de LaLiga Santander 2016/17|date=21 May 2017|work=laliga.es|access-date=22 May 2017|archive-date=12 July 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190712180825/http://www.laliga.es/noticias/real-madrid-campeon-de-laliga-santander-2016-17|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/39926301|title=Real Madrid win La Liga title with victory at Malaga|date=21 May 2017|publisher=BBC|access-date=12 February 2018|archive-date=11 December 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191211030150/https://www.bbc.com/sport/football/39926301|url-status=live}}</ref> he also started in the [[2017 UEFA Champions League Final|2016–17 UEFA Champions League final]] against [[Juventus FC|Juventus]] in [[Cardiff]], which Madrid won 4–1.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0250-0c5117c008df-de0901ea6dae-1000--majestic-real-madrid-win-champions-league-in-cardiff/|title=Majestic Real Madrid win Champions League in Cardiff|date=3 June 2017|publisher=UEFA|access-date=22 March 2025|archive-date=31 March 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190331042605/https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/season=2017/matches/round=2000787/match=2019641/postmatch/report/index.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 8 August 2017, Isco scored a goal in the [[2017 UEFA Super Cup]], contributing to Real Madrid's 2–1 victory against [[Manchester United F.C.|Manchester United]]. His performance earned him the man of the match award.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefasupercup/match/2022539--real-madrid-vs-man-utd/|title=UEFA Super Cup – Real Madrid C.F.-Man. United|last=UEFA.com|publisher=UEFA|language=en|access-date=28 August 2017|archive-date=22 August 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240822090605/https://www.uefa.com/uefasupercup/match/2022539--real-madrid-vs-man-utd/|url-status=live}}</ref> In September 2017, he signed a new deal with Real Madrid until June 2022.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2017/09/iscos-contract-extension|title=Isco's contract extension|date=14 September 2017|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.|access-date=14 September 2017|archive-date=28 February 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230228053045/https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2017/09/iscos-contract-extension|url-status=live}}</ref> During the [[2017–18 UEFA Champions League]], he made eleven appearances, when Madrid won their third consecutive and 13th overall Champions League title as they beat [[Liverpool FC|Liverpool]] 3–1 in [[Kyiv]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/news/0245-0e98d7318379-716954065574-1000--madrid-beat-liverpool-to-complete-hat-trick/|title=Madrid beat Liverpool to complete hat-trick|date=26 May 2018|publisher=UEFA|access-date=22 March 2025|archive-date=27 May 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180527203029/http://www.uefa.com/uefachampionsleague/season=2018/matches/round=2000885/match=2021711/postmatch/report/index.html|url-status=live}}</ref> He made 23 appearances during the league season, as Real Madrid won the [[2019–20 La Liga]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/real-madrid/2020/07/17/5f10db2146163f3c2c8b45d7.html|title=Real Madrid win the longest LaLiga Santander season|date=17 July 2020|access-date=17 July 2020|website=Marca|location=Spain|archive-date=18 July 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200718165201/https://www.marca.com/en/football/real-madrid/2020/07/17/5f10db2146163f3c2c8b45d7.html|url-status=live}}</ref> In the [[2021–22 Real Madrid CF season|2021–22]] season he was not an important player under [[Carlo Ancelotti]] as Real Madrid triumphed in [[2021–22 La Liga]] and the [[2021–22 UEFA Champions League]]. On 30 May 2022, Isco confirmed on social media that he was leaving the club after nine years.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Whitehead |first=Jacob |title=Isco announces Real Madrid exit |url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/4176543/2022/05/30/isco-announces-real-madrid-exit-this-summer-after-contract-expiration/ |access-date=30 May 2022 |website=The Athletic |archive-date=20 January 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250120041616/https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/4176543/2022/05/30/isco-announces-real-madrid-exit-this-summer-after-contract-expiration/ |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite web|date=1 June 2022|title=Official Announcement: Isco|url=https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2022/06/01/official-announcement-isco|publisher=Real Madrid CF|access-date=1 June 2022|archive-date=1 June 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220601232832/https://www.realmadrid.com/en/news/2022/06/01/official-announcement-isco|url-status=live}}</ref>

===Sevilla===
On 7 August 2022, [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla]] announced that the club reached an agreement in principle for the signing of Isco, with the player agreeing to a two-year contract.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://sevillafc.es/actualidad/noticias/principio-acuerdo-isco-alarcon|title=Principio de acuerdo con Isco Alarcón para su fichaje por el Sevilla FC|trans-title=Agreement in principle with Isco Alarcón for his signing with Sevilla FC|publisher=Sevilla FC|language=es|date=7 August 2022|accessdate=7 August 2022|archive-date=23 April 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260423003355/https://sevillafc.es/actualidad/noticias/principio-acuerdo-isco-alarcon|url-status=live}}</ref> On 21 December 2022, Isco and Sevilla agreed to terminate their contract.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2022-12-21 |title=Soccer-Sevilla part ways with Isco |language=en |work=Reuters |url=https://www.reuters.com/article/soccer-spain-sev-isco-idUKKBN2T50YH |access-date=2022-12-21 |archive-date=21 December 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221221191600/https://www.reuters.com/article/soccer-spain-sev-isco-idUKKBN2T50YH |url-status=live }}</ref> On 22 December, Sevilla coach [[Jorge Sampaoli]] said Isco "did not meet the club's expectations".<ref>{{Cite news |date=2022-12-22 |title=Isco failed to meet Sevilla's expectations, says Sampaoli |language=en |work=Reuters |url=https://www.reuters.com/lifestyle/sports/isco-failed-meet-sevillas-expectations-says-sampaoli-2022-12-22/ |access-date=2022-12-22}}</ref>

In the January transfer window, Isco came close to signing with [[Bundesliga]] club [[1. FC Union Berlin|Union Berlin]]. However, on 31 January 2023, the deal collapsed, despite him passing medical tests, as the German club claimed that he made new demands that differed from the original agreement.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.goal.com/en/news/union-berlin-confirm-isco-transfer-collapse-ex-real-madrid-completes-medical/blt8710dead699af786 |title='We have our limits!' - Union Berlin confirm Isco transfer collapse after ex-Real Madrid star completes medical |work=Goal.com |date=31 January 2023 |access-date=1 February 2023 |archive-date=27 July 2024 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240727045450/https://www.goal.com/en/news/union-berlin-confirm-isco-transfer-collapse-ex-real-madrid-completes-medical/blt8710dead699af786 |url-status=live }}</ref> However Isco’s representatives also claimed that Union Berlin has amended the contract the moment before Isco was going to sign it, in terms of both sporting terms and salary.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Kayser |first1=Carmen |last2=Vonholdt |first2=Florian |title=Neue Isco-Vorwürfe gegen Union |url=https://sportbild.bild.de/bundesliga/vereine/bundesliga/union-berlin-neue-isco-vorwuerfe-platzte-der-deal-deshalb-82750932.sport.html |website=[[Sport Bild]] |access-date=20 August 2025 |archive-url=https://archive.today/20250820025405/https://sportbild.bild.de/bundesliga/vereine/bundesliga/union-berlin-neue-isco-vorwuerfe-platzte-der-deal-deshalb-82750932.sport.html |archive-date=20 August 2025 |language=de |date=1 February 2023 |trans-title=New Isco allegations against Union}}</ref>

===Betis===
On 26 July 2023, Isco joined Sevilla's rivals [[Real Betis]] on a one-year deal.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://www.realbetisbalompie.es/noticias/actualidad/isco-nuevo-jugador-del-real-betis-balompie-29269 |title=Isco, nuevo jugador del Real Betis Balompié |trans-title=Isco, new player of Real Betis Balompié |publisher=Real Betis |date=26 July 2023 |access-date=26 July 2023 |language=Spanish |archive-date=19 January 2026 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260119182754/https://www.realbetisbalompie.es/noticias/actualidad/isco-nuevo-jugador-del-real-betis-balompie-29269 |url-status=live }}</ref> On 13 August 2023, during the opening matchday of La Liga, Isco played his first game for Betis, facing off against Villarreal.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Villarreal CF vs Real Betis - LALIGA EA SPORTS |url=https://www.laliga.com/en-GB/match/temporada-2023-2024-laliga-easports-villarreal-cf-real-betis-1 |access-date=2023-08-29 |website=LA LIGA EA SPORTS |language=es |archive-date=24 July 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230724201321/https://www.laliga.com/en-GB/match/temporada-2023-2024-laliga-easports-villarreal-cf-real-betis-1 |url-status=live }}</ref> Later, on 28 August, he netted his first goal for Betis when they played against [[Athletic Bilbao]], marking an end to his year-long absence from the scoresheet. However, despite his goal, Betis suffered a 4–2 defeat.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-08-28 |title=Athletic 4-2 Betis: results, summary and goals |url=https://en.as.com/resultados/futbol/primera/2023_2024/directo/regular_a_3_441122/ |access-date=2023-08-29 |website=AS US |language=en-us |archive-date=29 August 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230829071536/https://en.as.com/resultados/futbol/primera/2023_2024/directo/regular_a_3_441122/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

On 28 December 2023, Isco extended his contract with Betis until June 2027.<ref>{{Cite web |date=28 December 2023 |title=Isco renueva su contrato con el Real Betis |trans-title=Isco renews his contract with Real Betis |url=https://www.realbetisbalompie.es/noticias/actualidad/isco-renueva-su-contrato-con-el-real-betis-29748 |access-date=29 December 2023 |publisher=Real Betis Balompié |language=es-ES}}</ref> In the [[2023–24 La Liga|2023–24 season]], he was the player with most man of the match awards in La Liga, having received it in 19 occasions.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://getfootballnewsspain.com/how-many-man-of-the-match-awards-has-isco-received-with-real-betis-this-season/ |title=How many Man of the Match awards has Isco received with Real Betis this season? |publisher=Get Spanish Football News |date=13 May 2024 |access-date=5 July 2024 |archive-date=26 May 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250526105333/https://getfootballnewsspain.com/how-many-man-of-the-match-awards-has-isco-received-with-real-betis-this-season/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

In the 2024–2025 season, Isco led Real Betis to the [[2025 UEFA Conference League final|UEFA Europa Conference League Final]]—the club’s first-ever European final. On May 28, 2025, he assisted [[Abde Ezzalzouli|Abde Ezzalzouli’s]] opening goal, but Betis ultimately suffered a 4–1 defeat to Chelsea F.C in the final. Despite the loss, Isco was named the [[UEFA Europa League 2#Awards|UEFA Europa Conference League Player of the Season]]: [[2024–25 UEFA Europa Conference League#Player of the Season|2024–25]]<ref name="UCL player" />

==International career==
[[File:Francisco Román Alarcón Suárez.jpg|thumb|Isco in 2010]]

Isco appeared with [[Spain national under-17 football team|Spain's U17]] in [[2009 FIFA U-17 World Cup|2009 World Cup]], scoring three times in the process as the team finished third. In 2011, he represented [[Spain national under-20 football team|his country]] – together with Málaga teammate [[Recio (footballer)|Recio]] – in the [[2011 FIFA U-20 World Cup|U-20 World Cup]] held in [[Colombia]], netting one goal in an eventual quarter-final exit.

On 28 February 2012, Isco was called to the [[Spain national under-23 football team|Spain under-23s team]] for a [[Exhibition game#Association football|friendly]] against [[Egypt national under-23 football team|Egypt]], but did not leave the bench.<ref>[http://rfef.es/index.jsp?nodo=39&CATEGORIA=2&ID=4732 Convocatoria para el partido internacional olímpico España-Egipto (Spain-Egypt Olympic call-up)] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130801062400/http://rfef.es/index.jsp?nodo=39&CATEGORIA=2&ID=4732 |date=1 August 2013 }}; [[Royal Spanish Football Federation|RFEF]], 24 February 2012 {{in lang|es}}</ref> On 15 May he was picked for the first time to the [[Spain national football team|senior team]] for friendlies with [[Serbia national football team|Serbia]] and [[South Korea national football team|South Korea]], but took no part in either match. In July, he went with the under-23 team to the [[Football at the 2012 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|Olympics in London]],<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/olympics/18693622|title=Euro 2012 trio Mata, Alba & Martinez in Spain Olympic squad|work=BBC Sport|date=5 July 2012|access-date=4 November 2014|archive-date=11 October 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151011035055/http://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/0/olympics/18693622|url-status=live}}</ref> starting all of Spain's matches as they were eliminated without scoring a goal.

On 6 February 2013, Isco made his debut with the main squad, playing the last 30 minutes in a 3–1 win over [[Uruguay national football team|Uruguay]] in [[Doha]], Qatar.<ref>[http://www.marca.com/eventos/marcador/futbol/2012_13/amistosos_seleccion/4/spa_uru/ Campeón hasta en los simulacros (Champion even in drills)] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180710040817/http://www.marca.com/eventos/marcador/futbol/2012_13/amistosos_seleccion/4/spa_uru/ |date=10 July 2018 }}; ''Marca'' (Spain), 6 February 2013 {{in lang|es}}</ref> Also [[2013 UEFA European Under-21 Football Championship|that year]] he appeared at the [[UEFA European Under-21 Championship]] in [[2013 UEFA European Under-21 Championship|Israel]], he scored in the [[2013 UEFA European Under-21 Championship Final|final]] and finished the competition with the ''Bronze Boot'' (3 Goals) and made the team of the tournament as a key player for the eventual winners.<ref name=gb13>{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/under21/news/0257-0deccecab816-02cd0af34df4-1000--morata-wins-golden-boot-in-spanish-clean-sweep/|title=Morata wins Golden Boot in Spanish clean sweep|publisher=UEFA|date=18 June 2013|access-date=1 July 2017|last=Adams|first=Sam|quote=Bronze Boot: Isco, Spain – 3 goals|archive-date=18 April 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230418174802/https://www.uefa.com/under21/news/0257-0deccecab816-02cd0af34df4-1000--morata-wins-golden-boot-in-spanish-clean-sweep/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name="tot13">{{cite web|url=https://www.uefa.com/under21/news/0252-0cd3add5c6c6-33fdf8fdc07a-1000--thiago-leads-all-star-squad-dominated-by-spain/|title=Thiago leads all-star squad dominated by Spain|publisher=UEFA|date=21 June 2013|access-date=21 June 2013|archive-date=8 June 2026|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260608183644/https://www.uefa.com/under21/news/0252-0cd3add5c6c6-33fdf8fdc07a-1000--thiago-leads-all-star-squad-dominated-by-spain/|url-status=live}}</ref>

Isco scored his first international goal for Spain in a [[UEFA Euro 2016 qualifying]] match against [[Belarus national football team|Belarus]] in [[Huelva]] on 15 November 2014, opening a 3–0 win.<ref>{{cite news|last1=Hunter|first1=Graham|title=Much-changed Spain dominate Belarus|url=https://www.uefa.com/european-qualifiers/news/0253-0d7f8d20415a-6e68168eeaec-1000--much-changed-spain-dominate-belarus/|access-date=15 November 2014|publisher=UEFA|date=15 November 2014|archive-date=3 December 2014|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141203180443/http://www.uefa.com/uefaeuro/season=2016/matches/round=2000446/match=2013917/postmatch/report/index.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

Isco scored his first [[hat-trick]] for Spain on 27 March 2018, netting three goals against [[Argentina national football team|Argentina]] in a 6–1 friendly win.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.marca.com/en/football/spanish-football/2018/03/27/5abab523e5fdea7d498b4607.html|title=Spain smash Argentina for six|last1=Bell|first1=Arch|work=Marca|location=Spain|date=27 March 2018|access-date=27 March 2018|archive-date=28 March 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180328102728/http://www.marca.com/en/football/spanish-football/2018/03/27/5abab523e5fdea7d498b4607.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

In May 2018, Isco was named in Spain's final [[2018 FIFA World Cup squads|squad]] for the [[2018 FIFA World Cup]].<ref>{{cite web|title=Morata misses out on Spain's 23-man World Cup squad|url=http://www.goal.com/en/news/morata-misses-out-on-spain-world-cup-squad/1ub1qz7jod09i1lfvdcy84ea2l|date=21 May 2018|access-date=21 May 2018|archive-date=9 July 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190709141140/https://www.goal.com/en/news/morata-misses-out-on-spain-world-cup-squad/1ub1qz7jod09i1lfvdcy84ea2l|url-status=live}}</ref> He scored his first and only goal in the last [[2018 FIFA World Cup Group B|group stage match]] against [[Morocco national football team|Morocco]], in an eventual 2–2 draw. His goal helped the team to qualify to the second round as group winners.<ref>{{cite web |title=Spain Top Group After Thrilling Finale |publisher=FIFA |url=https://www.fifa.com/worldcup/archive/russia2018/matches/match/300340184/#match-summary |website=FIFA.com |date=25 June 2018 |access-date=15 June 2021 |archive-date=16 June 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210616043447/https://www.fifa.com/worldcup/archive/russia2018/matches/match/300340184/#match-summary |url-status=live }}</ref>

In May 2021, Isco was omitted from Spain's 26-man squad for [[UEFA Euro 2020]].<ref>{{cite news|title=Ramos reacts to shock Spain Euro 2020 squad omission: 'It hurts'|url=https://www.standard.co.uk/sport/football/sergio-ramos-spain-euro-2020-squad-omission-reaction-b936937.html|last=Flood|first=George|date=24 May 2021|work=Evening Standard|access-date=17 June 2021|archive-date=24 June 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210624205225/https://www.standard.co.uk/sport/football/sergio-ramos-spain-euro-2020-squad-omission-reaction-b936937.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

On 26 May 2025, Isco was recalled to the squad by manager [[Luis de la Fuente (footballer, born 1961)|Luis de la Fuente]] for the [[2025 UEFA Nations League Finals|UEFA Nations League Finals]] in Germany, marking his return after a six-year absence. In the final against [[Portugal national football team|Portugal]] on 8 June, he successfully converted his penalty attempt in a 5–3 shootout loss, following a 2–2 draw.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2025-05-26 |title=Squad list for the UEFA Nations League Final Four |url=https://rfef.es/en/noticias/call-up-list-for-the-uefa-nations-league-final-four |access-date=27 May 2025 |website=RFEF.es |publisher=[[Royal Spanish Football Federation]] |archive-date=26 May 2025 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250526183205/https://rfef.es/en/noticias/call-up-list-for-the-uefa-nations-league-final-four |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|date=26 May 2025|title=After 6-year absence, Isco returns to Spain's squad for Nations League semifinal. Rodri still out|url=https://apnews.com/article/rodri-isco-gavi-spain-nations-league-52b83d342c3023667424eea892a6edd7|access-date=27 May 2025|agency=[[Associated Press]]|archive-date=26 May 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250526175713/https://apnews.com/article/rodri-isco-gavi-spain-nations-league-52b83d342c3023667424eea892a6edd7|url-status=live}}</ref>

==Style of play==
[[File:Isco - Atletico Madrid 14.jpg|thumb|left|Isco is known for his dribbling ability.]]
Isco began his career as an [[Midfielder#Attacking midfielder|attacking midfielder]] or as a [[Forward (association football)#Second striker|second striker]]: at Málaga, under [[Manuel Pellegrini]], he often played in an [[Forward (association football)|attacking]] role in the team's 4–2–3–1 formation.<ref name="marca1">{{Cite web|url = http://www.marca.com/en/2015/02/25/en/football/real_madrid/1424853552.html|title = Isco, Ancelotti's go-to guy|date = 25 February 2015|access-date = 25 February 2015|work = Marca|location = Spain|archive-date = 26 February 2015|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20150226171818/http://www.marca.com/en/2015/02/25/en/football/real_madrid/1424853552.html|url-status = live}}</ref> Following his move to Real Madrid, manager [[Carlo Ancelotti]] also played him in a [[Midfielder#Deep-lying playmaker (Strolling 10)|deep-lying playmaker]] role requiring more sacrifice and defensive duties than his natural position.<ref name="marca1"/> He has also been deployed as a [[Forward (association football)#Winger|winger]] on occasion.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espnfc.us/club/real-madrid/86/blog/post/2738739/real-madrid-boss-rafa-benitez-has-james-isco-balancing-act|title=Real Madrid dealing with difficult James-Isco balancing act|publisher=ESPN FC|author1=Rob Train|date=3 December 2015|access-date=15 August 2016|archive-date=7 October 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161007130842/http://www.espnfc.us/club/real-madrid/86/blog/post/2738739/real-madrid-boss-rafa-benitez-has-james-isco-balancing-act|url-status=live}}</ref>

Isco is known for his ability to pick out a good pass, [[Dribbling#Association football|dribble]] or shoot into the top corner of the goal.<ref name="espn1">{{Cite web|url = http://www.espnfc.com/club/real-madrid/86/blog/post/2316993/iscos-rise-complicates-ancelottis-starting-lineup-at-real-madrid|title = Isco's rise complicates Ancelotti's starting lineup at Real Madrid|date = 25 February 2015|access-date = 25 February 2015|publisher = ESPN FC|archive-date = 26 February 2015|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20150226040754/http://www.espnfc.com/club/real-madrid/86/blog/post/2316993/iscos-rise-complicates-ancelottis-starting-lineup-at-real-madrid|url-status = live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.realmadrid.com/en/football/squad/francisco-roman--alarcon|title=For a footballer there is nothing greater than Real Madrid|publisher=Real Madrid C.F.|access-date=15 August 2016|archive-date=11 February 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210211134832/http://www.realmadrid.com/en/football/squad/francisco-roman--alarcon|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.goal.com/en/news/12/spanish-football/2015/03/20/10009662/marcelo-isco-is-madrids-most-impressive-player |title=Marcelo: Isco is Madrid's most impressive player |publisher=Goal.com |last1=Fryer |first1=Rupert |date=20 March 2015 |access-date=22 February 2019 |archive-date=23 February 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190223131530/https://www.goal.com/en/news/12/spanish-football/2015/03/20/10009662/marcelo-isco-is-madrids-most-impressive-player |url-status=live }}</ref> His reading of the game, his anticipation of space and the general directing of his side's performances are his most common traits.

In 2013, Isco was credited by [[Marca (newspaper)|''Marca'']] journalist Pablo Polo as being "the most promising young player in Spanish football", comparing his strength, skill, and low centre of gravity to [[Sergio Agüero]], and his vision and passing abilities to [[Zinedine Zidane]].<ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.marca.com/2013/06/28/en/football/real_madrid/1372403264.html|title=Zidane's class and Agüero's shimmy|work=Marca|location=Spain|author=Pablo Polo|date=28 June 2013|access-date=29 June 2013|archive-date=30 June 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130630121256/http://www.marca.com/2013/06/28/en/football/real_madrid/1372403264.html|url-status=live}}</ref> Former Real Madrid captain [[Iker Casillas]] predicted in 2015 that Isco would become Spain's most important player.<ref>{{cite news|title=Casillas: "Isco, el futuro jugador más importante de España"|trans-title=Casillas: "Isco, Spain's future most important player"|url=http://futbol.as.com/futbol/2015/02/22/primera/1424642534_544237.html|access-date=22 February 2015|publisher=Diario AS|date=22 February 2015|language=es|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150223002153/http://futbol.as.com/futbol/2015/02/22/primera/1424642534_544237.html|archive-date=23 February 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url = http://airherald.com/real-madrid-captain-iker-casillas-praises-performance-of-isco-but-warns-not-be-blinded-by-flattery/23001/|title = Real Madrid Captain Iker Casillas Praises Performance of Isco, But Warns Not Be Blinded By Flattery!|date = 25 February 2015|access-date = 25 February 2015|website = Air Herald|last = Roshanzadeh|first = Ahmad|archive-url = https://web.archive.org/web/20150225014741/http://airherald.com/real-madrid-captain-iker-casillas-praises-performance-of-isco-but-warns-not-be-blinded-by-flattery/23001/|archive-date = 25 February 2015|url-status = dead}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Isco dated Victoria Calderon; the couple had a son.<ref>{{cite journal |title=Isco and Sara Salamo welcome their first child into the world |journal=Marca |date=11 July 2017 |url=https://www.marca.com/en/football/real-madrid/2019/07/11/5d2745a8ca474116658b45a3.html |archive-date=15 January 2023 |access-date=15 January 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230115220120/https://www.marca.com/en/football/real-madrid/2019/07/11/5d2745a8ca474116658b45a3.html |url-status=live }}</ref> He has two more sons with actress [[Sara Sálamo]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Isco's Partner Revealed They Have A 'Competitive' Sex Life |url=https://www.sportbible.com/football/iscos-partner-revealed-they-have-a-competitive-sex-life-20220802 |website=sportbible.com |date=2 August 2022 |publisher=Sport bible |access-date=15 January 2023 |archive-date=15 January 2023 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230115212924/https://www.sportbible.com/football/iscos-partner-revealed-they-have-a-competitive-sex-life-20220802 |url-status=live }}</ref>
